Subject: Capacity options — need a pragmatic path to production

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and routing features look promising. We need to lock down a dedicated plan tied to our upcoming pilot (internal deadline: Jan 15). Our infra team is focused on predictable baseline throughput for inference-heavy batch jobs during business hours with occasional burst windows.

Could you share 2–3 proposal variants that balance cost and activation speed? Specifically:
- cluster size options (GPUs) and the minimum committed GPUs for SLAs
- a realistic ramp schedule (30/60/90-day style) and warmup credits
- fallback/overflow strategy if we hit burst above reserved capacity

If useful, Samir can send our QPS profiles and peak sequence-length distribution. Looking for a short doc we can review with procurement next week.

Best,
Ava Collins
Head of AI Integrations
Orchard Health

PS — we may need SOC2 evidence during contract review; can that follow the pricing doc?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity options — need a pragmatic path to production

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a compact proposal with three distinct reservation variants and an activation timeline spreadsheet ("gpu-slate-activation.xlsx"). High level:

Variant A — Minimum Baseline (cost-efficient)
- Committed: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Activation (30 days): onboarding + warm cache; SLA: 99.5% for p95 token latency
- Burst: 2x burst pool (best-effort) with preemptible instances
- Warmup credits: 50k token credits to offset cold-starts

Variant B — Production Ready (balanced)
- Committed: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Activation (45 days): phased ramp with canary and fleet warm starts
- Burst: 3x guaranteed burst capacity via reserved burst lanes
- Warmup credits: 150k token credits + early prewarming windows

Variant C — High Throughput (SLA-first)
- Committed: 32x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Activation (60–90 days): staged activation by region, dedicated prewarm nodes
- Burst: 4x guaranteed burst + cross-region failover
- Warmup credits: 500k tokens; priority scheduling during business hours

Key trade-offs: lower-commitment plans rely on preemptible burst for cost savings; higher commitments reduce variability and give better cold-start economics. I called out typical per-token pricing for each vector in the attached PDF.

Next steps I propose:
1) Samir shares the QPS / seq length CSV (we’ll run a quick sizing simulation).
2) We align on preferred variant so we can draft a procurement-ready SOW and include SOC2 evidence.
3) If you want, we can provision a short pilot (2–4 GPUs reserved) to validate warmup behavior before full activation.

Looping karthik and Ben for sizing and activation cadence input.

-M

--

Marissa / team — quick tech note to support Ava's ask (I've sketched assumptions in the sheet):

- If their peak seq lengths are >2k for a subset of requests, recommend Variant B as a minimum; the extra memory footprint materially changes packing and KV cache sizing.
- For Variant A we should prescribe a mandatory prefix caching policy and a 15% steady-state overprovision buffer to keep p95 latency in target during business-hours QPS spikes.
- Ramp schedule:
  * Day 0–14: staging and canary (1–2 nodes live, traffic split 5–10%)
  * Day 15–30: warm-up + increase reservation to 50% of committed capacity; monitor token-cost and tail latency
  * Day 31–45: full activation to committed profile (for Variant B)
- Warmup credits: convert token credits into scheduled prewarm windows (2 x 2-hour warmups during business hours per week for first 6 weeks) — this helps KV cache hitrate quickly.
- Overflow: recommend a soft-fallback chain: first route to reserved burst lanes, then to compatible 8-bit quantized model variants (cost cheaper), finally best-effort preemptible fleet. Document these fallback SLAs in the SOW.

Ben — can you add the expected cost delta for enabling guaranteed burst lanes vs best-effort? Priyom — can you add a one-page onboarding checklist (drive link in the offer) showing who signs off on network/VPC, key rotation, and SOC2 artifact handoff?

Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect

- Burst lanes: enable 2x guaranteed burst lanes for business-hour peaks (adds ~12% to monthly commit cost)

Thanks — looking forward to getting Orchard Health into production.
